benchmarks.summary: This is a deliberately broad question ("target benchmarks AND development proxies") and the GOLD answers it as a full-evolution survey across 2024-2026: during-training MCQ/lm-eval-harness tier (#574/#817), Delphi scaling-law pre-registration proxy (#1337, verified 2.75/2.55/2.40 → 2.758/2.53), the live Table-9 DSP mixture-selection objective (#6608/#6611/#6726), AA Intelligence Index v4.0.4 target framework (#5819), executed Evalchemy generative subset (#2779), downstream-scaling proxies (#4550), Qwen comparator (61.96 vs 64.66, verified) and the 67B loss target (2.269 in #6044, not #6811 — verified). The gold is accurate, well-verified, and carefully stratified (target vs executed, achieved vs projected); it is very long but I found no material overreach. A (skill) gives a coherent, correct MODERN-strategic framing (AA index target + perplexity-gap proxy + #4550 + Qwen + 67B loss) but genuinely omits three real tiers: the during-training MCQ/harness tier, the Delphi pre-registration mechanism, and the Table-9 DSP objective; it also miscites evalchemy to #5819 (which does not name evalchemy). B (repo baseline) correctly describes the static task_configs.py menu (CORE_TASKS, key_evals OLMo2-comparable, leaderboard, Harbor agentic) and the in-loop bpb/logprob/choice metrics + proxy-research threads — real content the gold under-covers — but is disconnected from the 2026 live state (no AA index, no Table-9, no Delphi numbers, no evalchemy, no Qwen numbers, no 67B target). CRITICAL SCORING BUG: fact-6 regex `Table.9|table9|51` — the bare `51` matched issue #4551 (B) and #5519 (A), giving BOTH a false-positive pass on the Table-9 objective they never discuss. This over-credited both. Correcting it: A fact_cov 5/13→4/13 (~Q51), B fact_cov 2/13→1/13 (~Q36), the latter roughly offset by a citation-equivalence under-credit where B sources the CORE tier to task_configs.py rather than #574. Net: both Q values land close to fair after the two errors cancel. A ~fair (slightly lenient), B ~fair.

The one scoring error is too-LENIENT, not too-harsh: the fact-6 `51` regex false-positived on issue #5519, crediting A with Table-9 content it lacks (fact_cov should be 4/13=0.308, not 0.385), lowering fair Q to ~51.

Replace with something context-bound, e.g. `OLMoBaseEval|Table.?9|51[- ]?(component|BPB|task)`. After the fix BOTH A and B correctly FAIL fact 6.

For must-have #574 (CORE/default_eval tier), accept the canonical source `experiments/evals/task_configs.py` or issue #553 as an equivalent citation, so a repo-grounded answer that correctly names CORE_TASKS is not zeroed on sourcing alone.

h100-67b.summary: GOLD is solid and accurate — I verified its load-bearing numbers against the frozen corpus: 19.9% MFU on 4 nodes SGD/Adam with 'Muon needs to go' (#6693/#gpu June 26), MuonH5 4.7499 vs SGD 16.1876 MFU (#6493), the 63-74 GiB first-step OOM (#6367), the TPU pivot with 18.6% sustained on resume15k_v2 (July summary/#6044/#6811), the 26.7->26.5% flat weak-scale + 3.7pt Muon give-back + 50.3/56.2 ceilings, JaxPP 18.26% / 'Hopper is back on the menu' (#7024), fused-EP #6597, 23.8% d2048 POC (#6716), B200 17.8%, and #4302 superseded. Gold correctly distinguishes the 18.6% final TPU number from the 21.54% v4-1024 per-chip best — a distinction BOTH A and B get wrong (they stop at ~21.5%). A (skill+frozen, Q=87.7) is a strong, correct, well-hedged answer whose fact failures are almost all genuine gaps (it omits the July JaxPP revival, the roofline ceilings, and the 18.6% TPU final); only fact #2 ('four nodes' vs regex '4 nodes') is unfairly scored, ~1.5 pts — verdict fair, fair Q ~89. B (no-skill live, Q=70.4) genuinely misses the June 19.9% production headline, the Muon tax numbers, the TPU final, and the July PP work; all nine failed-fact deductions are fair, but two of its PASSING facts (#5 '4.75' matched '74.75 GiB', #6 'all-gather' matched a weak-scaling line) are false-positive regex credits inflating Q ~3 pts — offset by the scorer's inability to reward B's accurate live-#6979 depth (28.16% GQA, fast-EP landscape, 'moving to B200'). Net B verdict fair, fair Q ~70. Main scorer fixes: anchor the '4.75' and 'all-gather' regexes (currently too lenient to B), accept spelled-out 'four nodes' (too harsh to A), and relax the unfetchable #7024 must-have under the frozen condition.

inference.summary: GOLD is solid (~89): comprehensive, accurate on every spot-check (6709=ihodes, 6500=penfever, 6335 GH200/Jupiter job 849580, 5285/5400/5887 Iris substrate, 6042 DoD, 2.5hr/step), handles the subtle 'RL step wall-clock != serving throughput' and 'GH200 Jupiter != CoreWeave H100' distinctions correctly, and is transparent about provenance. Its one real gap is omitting #6136 (throughput-vs-quality decode corruption), which the baseline B actually caught. A (skill, Q=64) is a strong, accurate but narrower answer whose deductions are mostly FAIR — it genuinely omits the Iris serving substrate, the role epic (6500/6626/6627), and conflates MarinSkyRL as CoreWeave H100 while dropping the GH200/Jupiter history; scoring is fair with only ~5 pts of softness (marginal must-haves 2237/4401, strict 'Iris inference service' regex); fair Q ~67. B (baseline, Q=47) is scored slightly too harsh: it validly cited real content the gold ignored (#6136 corruption bug, #1898 Levanter epic) for no credit (~6 pts unfair), but genuinely earns a low score via a factual error (#6709 attributed to yonromai, actually ihodes), omitting the headline current-perf number, and missing the GrugMoE close-outs/EP8; fair Q ~53. True quality: gold 89, A 78, B 60.
